title: Styles
tab_intro: Give the model a reusable writing style — register, rhythm, imagery, dialogue conventions — extracted from books you already like or from a quick sample translation. Assign one below (or via Settings → Translation Options) to apply it to every chunk.
unassign_title: Currently assigned to translation — click to unassign
confirm_overwrite: A style named "{{name}}" already exists. Overwrite it?
list_empty_message: No styles yet. Extract one from books or start from a blank style.
context_hint: The world the text takes place in: period, technological level, social frame. This is what keeps the translation from reaching for a word that belongs to another era. Leave empty when it does not apply.
context_placeholder: A pre-industrial secondary world: sword combat, no gunpowder, a feudal social order
manual_edits_warning: Editing the text below directly disconnects it from the rules above. Use "Reassemble from rules" to regenerate it from the checked rules.
extract_intro: Pick one or more books. The model reads sample excerpts and proposes a set of style rules — register, rhythm, imagery, dialogue conventions — that you can review before creating a reusable style.
extract_dropzone: Drop files here or click to browse
mode_source_hint: The books you upload are the text you are about to translate — the rules keep the translation reading like the original.
mode_model_hint: The books you upload are a stylistic model — an unrelated text will be translated to read like them.
candidates_hint: Uncheck any rule you don't want to keep.
evidence_tooltip: Evidence from the source text supporting this rule
too_many_files: Too many files selected. Maximum is {{max}}.
flagged_hint: Flagged rules quote the book directly or name specific words — reusing them makes the model repeat that vocabulary.
abstraction_notice: Rules that name specific words or quote the book are unchecked — reusing them makes the model repeat that vocabulary throughout the translation. Rewrite them abstractly or leave them out.
